note: Nivolumab reached SCLC on a rat surrogate in non-SCLC syngeneic tumours and clean cynomolgus toxicology; CheckMate 032's 10 % response matched in direction, CheckMate 331 then failed overall survival, monkeys missed the immune-related harms the PD-1 knockout mouse foretold, the CheckMate 032 tumour-mutational-burden rule held in CheckMate 451, and the Rb1/Trp53 SCLC mouse that reproduces monotherapy inertness arrived after the clinic knew; toripalimab's chemotherapy-combination win (EXTENTORCH) is listed but, by this run's rule, not credited to a model that dosed the antibody alone.
label: SCLC (anti-PD-1)

engagement.magnitude_basis: in-vitro high-affinity PD-1 binding and ligand blockade on human T cells (no occupancy percentage in the abstract) vs sustained mean occupancy >70 % of PD-1 on circulating T cells in dosed patients at 0.3-10 mg/kg
engagement.population: Melanoma, colorectal, prostate, non-small-cell lung and renal cancer phase 1 patients (not SCLC)
engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading of both papers. The patient occupancy was measured in Brahmer 2010 before the in-vitro characterisation was published (Wang 2014), so 2014 is the year both sides were public; engagement does not require the context disease. Europe PMC renders the quote with '> 70%'; PubMed may set it as '>70%'. The FDA 2014 pharmacology review tabulates monkey receptor occupancy (its Table 16) but the scraped text did not carry the values.
engagement.model: In-vitro PD-1 binding and ligand-blockade characterisation of nivolumab on human T cells, with cynomolgus PD-1 binding (nivolumab does not bind rodent PD-1)
engagement.note: Nivolumab's in-vitro PD-1 binding and blockade was matched by >70 % PD-1 occupancy on circulating T cells in dosed patients, sustained two months at every dose.
engagement.short: Patient PD-1 occupancy >70% as in vitro
engagement.quote: However, pharmacodynamics indicated a sustained mean occupancy of > 70% of PD-1 molecules on circulating T cells
engagement.judgement: Pairing is mine: the model side is nivolumab's in-vitro PD-1 binding and ligand-blockade work (Wang 2014, the characterisation the BLA filed), the patient side the phase 1 occupancy readout. Scored same in direction: the readout the model used (PD-1 occupancy on T cells) moved in dosed humans. Patients were not SCLC; no SCLC trial measured occupancy. The same track as the HCC tile's in-vitro occupancy titration, because both systems are cell-based occupancy predictions; the cynomolgus occupancy table in the FDA review could not be read from the scrape, so the monkey is not scored here.

engagement.magnitude_basis: in-vitro saturation of PD-1 on circulating T cells above 3 ug/mL vs population-PK steady-state troughs of 35.6 ug/mL (3 mg/kg Q2W) and 24.1 ug/mL (240 mg Q3W): 8-12-fold above the saturating concentration
engagement.population: Toripalimab monotherapy population across tumour types (phase 1 and nasopharyngeal carcinoma; not SCLC)
engagement.confidence_note: Review clinical pharmacology passages read (bundle text around pp. 5589-5610, 8668-8676 and 9140-9165 of the extracted file). The review says the saturating concentration was measured in vitro on circulating T cells obtained during the phase 1 studies; whether occupancy was also read in vivo under dosing is not stated in the passages read, so the human side is concentration-based.
engagement.model: In-vitro PD-1 receptor-occupancy titration of toripalimab on circulating human T cells (complete occupancy above 3 ug/mL; 20 ug/mL chosen for the tumour microenvironment), with occupancy-saturated cynomolgus toxicology
engagement.note: FDA set the in-vitro saturating concentration beside patient exposures: steady-state troughs of 24-36 ug/mL on both regimens, far above the 3 ug/mL that saturates PD-1 on T cells.
engagement.quote: It is notable that full receptor occupancy is achieved in the peripheral blood mononuclear cells at much lower concentrations than that achieved with the proposed dosage regimens.
engagement.reason: Occupancy readout reached in dosed patients
engagement.judgement: Strengthens the 2014 entry rather than a new status: a second member, product-dosed, with the regulator stating the comparison in one section (comparison_stated true). The regimen EXTENTORCH used in SCLC (240 mg Q3W) is one of the two the review covers. Camrelizumab's phase 1 also measured patient occupancy, but no model-side number was found to pair it with, so it is noted, not scored.

dose.confidence_note: Review text obtained through the fc.py scrape of the FDA pharmacology review (memorandum dated 2014-12-04); the executive-summary sentence is verbatim. The review also states monkey exposures were up to 42-fold the clinical AUC of 25,500 ug*h/mL at 3 mg/kg Q2W.
dose.model: Cynomolgus monkey 4-week (weekly) and 13-week (twice-weekly) repeat-dose toxicology of nivolumab (up to 50 mg/kg; exposures at every dose above the 3 mg/kg Q2W clinical exposure)
dose.note: Monkeys tolerated 50 mg/kg with only diffuse inflammatory infiltrates; exposures at every dose exceeded the human 3 mg/kg Q2W exposure. No SCLC patient yet dosed.
dose.short: Monkey margin stated; SCLC not yet dosed
dose.quote: In both monkey studies, exposure of nivolumab at all dose levels tested exceeded that measured in humans at the intended clinical dose and schedule of 3 mg/kg once every 2 weeks.
dose.judgement: Opens the monkey track at the BLA: the filed model stated a tolerated exposure far above the clinical one. The SCLC dose (3 mg/kg Q2W in CheckMate 032, 240 mg Q2W in CheckMate 331) was inherited from this margin and from non-SCLC occupancy work; no SCLC-specific exposure-response against a model exists.

dose.magnitude_basis: monkey exposures up to 42-fold the clinical AUC at 3 mg/kg Q2W, the dose CheckMate 032 used; grade 3-4 treatment-related events 13 % on nivolumab 3 mg/kg
dose.population: Relapsed limited- or extensive-stage SCLC after platinum (CheckMate 032 nivolumab 3 mg/kg cohort)
dose.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading of Antonia 2016 (Lancet Oncol, epub 2016-06-04). Single-arm phase 1/2 with objective response as primary endpoint and no stated null hypothesis; 'worked' rests on the authors' reading and on the response rate the FDA later accepted. NCT01928394 results posted 2020-03-24.
dose.model: Cynomolgus monkey 4-week (weekly) and 13-week (twice-weekly) repeat-dose toxicology of nivolumab (up to 50 mg/kg; exposures at every dose above the 3 mg/kg Q2W clinical exposure)
dose.note: SCLC patients were dosed at the model's 3 mg/kg Q2W target without the (absent) monkey toxicity; nivolumab alone gave a 10 % objective response, durable in responders.
dose.short: Target dose reached; 10% ORR in CheckMate 032
dose.quote: An objective response was achieved in ten (10%) of 98 patients receiving nivolumab 3 mg/kg
dose.judgement: Reached-and-worked rule with decision 16, tied to the efficacy entry of the same year: the monkey stated a tolerated exposure (50 mg/kg, up to 42-fold the clinical AUC) and SCLC patients were dosed to the 3 mg/kg Q2W target without that toxicity, so margin_stated true. Low confidence because the efficacy signal it is tied to is a 10 % single-arm response rate. Pairing is mine. The nivolumab plus ipilimumab cohorts are not scored: the monkey never dosed the combination.

dose.population: Relapsed SCLC after first-line platinum (CheckMate 331, nivolumab 240 mg Q2W vs topotecan or amrubicin)
dose.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading of Spigel 2021 (Ann Oncol, epub 2021-02-01). NCT02481830 results posted 2020-01-09, which sets the year. The withdrawal of the US SCLC indication (announced by the sponsor in December 2020) is later knowledge noted only as confirmation that no higher dose was tried.
dose.model: Cynomolgus monkey 4-week (weekly) and 13-week (twice-weekly) repeat-dose toxicology of nivolumab (up to 50 mg/kg; exposures at every dose above the 3 mg/kg Q2W clinical exposure)
dose.note: Nivolumab 240 mg Q2W, the exposure the monkey margin covered, failed overall survival against chemotherapy in 569 relapsed-SCLC patients; no higher dose was tried.
dose.quote: No significant improvement in OS was seen with nivolumab versus chemotherapy [median OS, 7.5 versus 8.4 months; hazard ratio (HR), 0.86; 95% confidence interval (CI), 0.72-1.04; P = 0.11].
dose.reason: Reached, failed, abandoned: derived from efficacy
dose.judgement: Reached-failed-abandoned rule: the exposure target was met (240 mg Q2W is the 3 mg/kg-equivalent flat dose, occupancy saturating at every dose tested in Brahmer 2010), the primary endpoint failed, and no higher nivolumab dose was pursued in SCLC, so contra derived_from efficacy and counted once. The tolerability margin itself held (grade 3-4 treatment-related events 13.8 % vs 73.2 % on chemotherapy), so margin_stated stays true; the harms the monkey missed are scored in safety. CheckMate 451 (maintenance nivolumab, OS HR 0.84, 95 % CI 0.69-1.02, a secondary endpoint; combination arm not scored) points the same way. Toripalimab's EXTENTORCH success at 240 mg Q3W sits on the in-silico regimen track below and, under this run's combination rule, is not credited; the track cannot turn back without patient_signal_reversed in any case.

dose.confidence_note: Review dosing passages read (extracted file around lines 9140-9165). The EXTENTORCH patient side (Cheng 2025, JAMA Oncol, epub 2024-11-14, doi 10.1001/jamaoncol.2024.5019: OS HR 0.80, 95 % CI 0.65-0.98, P = .03 for toripalimab 240 mg Q3W plus etoposide-platinum vs placebo plus etoposide-platinum) was read at abstract level; NCT04012606 has no posted results (checked 2026-11-05).
dose.model: Population-PK comparison of toripalimab 3 mg/kg Q2W and 240 mg Q3W against the 20 ug/mL trough chosen to keep PD-1 saturated in the tumour microenvironment (simulated troughs 35.6 and 24.1 ug/mL)
dose.note: The 240 mg Q3W regimen EXTENTORCH used holds troughs above the 20 ug/mL occupancy target; the trial met OS, but as an add-on to chemotherapy.
dose.short: 240 mg Q3W holds target; combination uncredited
dose.quote: Toripalimab 3 mg/kg IV Q2W and 240 mg IV Q3W both achieve trough levels above 20 µg/mL and these two trials provide evidence of safety and effectiveness with both treatment regimens.
dose.reason: Combination trial; model dosed antibody alone
dose.judgement: Its own track, as in the HCC tile: an in-silico regimen model with no tolerability output, kept apart from the monkey. The only SCLC test of this regimen is EXTENTORCH, a placebo-controlled add-on to etoposide-platinum; under this run's rule that combination trials credit the antibody only when the model dosed the combination, it does not score, so the entry stays untested and EXTENTORCH is recorded in the efficacy cell's patient_trials. Judgement call for the reviewer: the placebo-controlled design isolates the antibody's contribution, and under an isolated-contribution reading this entry and the efficacy track's toripalimab datum would both be same (reached, worked). Toripalimab's monkey NOAEL (100 mg/kg weekly for 26 weeks, occupancy saturated) is on the monkey track by identity but is not entered, because the track is already contra and the same combination rule applies.

efficacy.confidence_note: Review text obtained through the fc.py scrape (about 60 kB of the review); the study list names J558 myeloma, MC38 colon, SA1/N fibrosarcoma and B16-F10 models. The v2 checker, reading the full PDF, recorded that RENCA, 4T1, CT26 and B16F10 were refractory to 4H2 and only J558, MC38 and SA1/N responded; that passage was not in the scraped text and is reported on the checker's authority.
efficacy.model: Syngeneic mouse transplants (J558 myeloma, MC38 colon carcinoma, SA1/N fibrosarcoma responsive; renal, breast, colon CT26 and B16-F10 melanoma refractory) dosed with 4H2, a rat-derived chimeric anti-mouse PD-1 surrogate, because nivolumab does not bind rodent PD-1
efficacy.note: The filed model: a surrogate antibody delayed non-SCLC syngeneic tumours in 3 of 7 lines. No SCLC model was filed; CheckMate 032 opened in 2013 on this.
efficacy.short: Surrogate active in 3 of 7 non-SCLC tumours
efficacy.quote: This murine surrogate for nivolumab exhibited anti-tumor activity in multiple murine syngeneic tumors models.
efficacy.judgement: Opens the filed-model track. The surrogate is a sibling, not a member (product_in_model false); the tumours are not SCLC, so the system predicts class activity, not SCLC biology. Toripalimab's product-dosed MC38 in human PD-1 knock-in mice is a different system and carries its own track (hpd1-knockin-mc38, split at the model-sweep merge).

efficacy.magnitude_basis: tumour growth delay with a surrogate in 3 of 7 syngeneic non-SCLC lines vs 10 % objective response (10 of 98) on nivolumab 3 mg/kg in relapsed SCLC
efficacy.population: Relapsed limited- or extensive-stage SCLC after platinum (CheckMate 032, nivolumab 3 mg/kg cohort)
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading of Antonia 2016 (Lancet Oncol, epub 2016-06-04). Single-arm phase 1/2, investigator-assessed objective response as primary endpoint, no stated null hypothesis; the quote is a verbatim clause of a longer sentence. NCT01928394 results posted 2020-03-24. The later third-line (Ready 2019) and randomised-cohort (Ready 2020) reports are listed, not scored.

patient_trials.quote: the objective response rate was 11.9% (95% confidence interval: 6.5-19.5) with a median duration of response of 17.9 months (range 3.0-42.1)
ORR increased with nivolumab plus ipilimumab (21.9% versus 11.6% with nivolumab; odds ratio: 2.12; 95% confidence interval: 1.06-4.26; p = 0.03).

efficacy.model: Syngeneic mouse transplants (J558 myeloma, MC38 colon carcinoma, SA1/N fibrosarcoma responsive; renal, breast, colon CT26 and B16-F10 melanoma refractory) dosed with 4H2, a rat-derived chimeric anti-mouse PD-1 surrogate, because nivolumab does not bind rodent PD-1
efficacy.note: Nivolumab alone gave objective responses in 10 % of 98 relapsed-SCLC patients, durable in responders: single-agent activity as the surrogate predicted, if weak.
efficacy.quote: An objective response was achieved in ten (10%) of 98 patients receiving nivolumab 3 mg/kg
efficacy.judgement: Same in direction, partial: the model predicted single-agent anti-tumour activity and a member showed some, with durable responses, on the trial's primary endpoint; a mouse growth delay and a response rate share no scale. Not neg: the filed data did not fall below a class bar for SCLC (the refractory lines were other tumours, and nothing in the package addressed SCLC). The nivolumab plus ipilimumab cohorts (ORR 19-23 %) are not credited because the model never dosed the combination. Low confidence: a 10 % response rate in a single-arm study is weak evidence of agreement, and a reviewer preferring untested until the randomised test can move the status to the 2020 entry.

efficacy.population: Unselected (rule proposes the upper tumour-mutational-burden tertile)
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading of Hellmann 2018 (Cancer Cell, epub 2018-05-03). The rule was derived retrospectively from whole-exome sequencing of CheckMate 032 patients (nivolumab alone and with ipilimumab), so it is not scored on the cohort that produced it; NCT01928394 results posted 2020-03-24. Tumour whole-exome sequencing as a selection rule has no exact model_kind; human_genetic is the nearest enum.
efficacy.model: Tumour-mutational-burden patient-selection rule from whole-exome sequencing of CheckMate 032 SCLC tumours (high tertile predicts benefit from nivolumab with or without ipilimumab)
efficacy.note: A patient-level rule proposed from CheckMate 032: high tumour mutational burden enriches for response to nivolumab, more so with ipilimumab. No prospective test yet.
efficacy.quote: Efficacy of nivolumab ± ipilimumab was enhanced in patients with high tumor mutational burden.
efficacy.judgement: The patient-level track the brief asks for: a selection rule built on patient data, so its first entry is untested until a later trial applies it prospectively. Not a retrodiction entry because it is scored only on later trials (decision 10). Not filed: the 2018 accelerated approval and the label carried no TMB selection.

efficacy.magnitude_basis: surrogate tumour growth delay in syngeneic non-SCLC mice vs OS HR 0.86 (95 % CI 0.72-1.04, P = 0.11), ORR 13.7 % vs 16.5 %, PFS HR 1.41 for nivolumab vs chemotherapy
efficacy.population: Relapsed SCLC after first-line platinum (CheckMate 331, nivolumab 240 mg Q2W vs topotecan or amrubicin, n = 569)
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading of Spigel 2021 (Ann Oncol, epub 2021-02-01); NCT02481830 results posted 2020-01-09 set the year. CheckMate 451 (Owonikoko 2021, full text read in passages; NCT02538666 results posted 2019-10-22) and EXTENTORCH (Cheng 2025, abstract) are listed. Camrelizumab's SCLC trials (PASSION, camrelizumab plus apatinib, NCT03417895, results posted 2024-08-07; camrelizumab plus platinum-irinotecan, NCT04453930, Frontiers 2023; induction chemotherapy then camrelizumab, apatinib and etoposide-carboplatin, NCT05001412, 2025) are all single-arm combinations with apatinib or chemotherapy and were not read beyond abstracts or registry, so they are noted, not listed.

patient_trials.quote: The HR for OS with nivolumab versus placebo was 0.84 (95% CI, 0.69 to 1.02); the median OS for nivolumab was 10.4 months.

Compared with placebo, toripalimab improved investigator-assessed PFS (hazard ratio [HR], 0.67 [95% CI, 0.54-0.82]; P < .001), and significantly reduced the risk of death (HR, 0.80 [95% CI, 0.65-0.98]; P = .03).

efficacy.model: Syngeneic mouse transplants (J558 myeloma, MC38 colon carcinoma, SA1/N fibrosarcoma responsive; renal, breast, colon CT26 and B16-F10 melanoma refractory) dosed with 4H2, a rat-derived chimeric anti-mouse PD-1 surrogate, because nivolumab does not bind rodent PD-1
efficacy.note: CheckMate 331: nivolumab alone did not beat chemotherapy on overall survival in relapsed SCLC (HR 0.86, P = 0.11); the surrogate-tumour prediction failed its randomised test.
efficacy.short: CheckMate 331 missed OS; indication later withdrawn
efficacy.quote: No significant improvement in OS was seen with nivolumab versus chemotherapy [median OS, 7.5 versus 8.4 months; hazard ratio (HR), 0.86; 95% confidence interval (CI), 0.72-1.04; P = 0.11].
efficacy.reason: Generic tumours wrong for SCLC monotherapy
efficacy.judgement: Contra on the filed-model track: a randomised phase 3 primary endpoint failed for a member given alone, which beats the 2016 single-arm agreement. CheckMate 451's nivolumab-alone arm (OS HR 0.84, CI crossing 1, a hierarchically tested secondary) is listed as the second miss; its nivolumab plus ipilimumab primary (HR 0.92, P = .37) is not scored because the model never dosed the combination. EXTENTORCH (toripalimab 240 mg Q3W plus etoposide-platinum vs placebo plus etoposide-platinum; PFS HR 0.67, OS HR 0.80) is listed and is the judgement call of this tile: under this run's rule that combination trials credit the antibody only when the model dosed the combination, and because toripalimab's filed MC38 knock-in model (FDA review 2023, its own track hpd1-knockin-mc38) dosed toripalimab alone, it does not turn the track; the lint also forbids contra to same without patient_signal_reversed. Under an isolated-contribution reading (placebo-controlled add-on) it would be same for the class. Pembrolizumab, atezolizumab, durvalumab and serplulimab are not members and are not scored.

efficacy.magnitude_basis: rule: high-TMB tertile benefits more; CheckMate 451 at the prespecified 13 mut/Mb cutoff: OS HR 0.61 (0.39-0.94) for nivolumab plus ipilimumab and 0.67 (0.45-1.01) for nivolumab vs placebo above the cutoff, 1.04 and 0.92 below; the 10 mut/Mb cutoff was not predictive
efficacy.population: Extensive-disease SCLC without progression after first-line chemotherapy, TMB-evaluable subset (580 of 834; 191 with TMB at or above 13 mut/Mb)
efficacy.confidence_note: Full text of Owonikoko 2021 (JCO, epub 2021-03-08; PMC8078251) read in passages. The TMB subgroup was prespecified in cutoff but exploratory; the registry record (results posted 2019-10-22) is not expected to carry the TMB subgroup, so the paper sets the year. CheckMate 331's abstract reports no TMB analysis and its full text was not read. The Hellmann rule used whole-exome missense tertiles; CheckMate 451 used a targeted panel in mut/Mb, so the scales differ.
efficacy.model: Tumour-mutational-burden patient-selection rule from whole-exome sequencing of CheckMate 032 SCLC tumours (high tertile predicts benefit from nivolumab with or without ipilimumab)
efficacy.note: CheckMate 451, prespecified cutoffs: above 13 mut/Mb nivolumab plus ipilimumab improved OS (HR 0.61) and nivolumab trended (HR 0.67); below it neither did; 10 mut/Mb failed.
efficacy.quote: A trend toward OS benefit with nivolumab plus ipilimumab was observed in patients with tumor mutational burden ≥ 13 mutations per megabase.
efficacy.judgement: Same, partial: the rule's direction held in a prospective trial that failed overall, for the combination (significant) and for nivolumab alone (trend, CI 0.45-1.01). The combination is credited here because the rule itself was derived on nivolumab with and without ipilimumab, so the model dosed the combination. The paper puts the CheckMate 032 rule and its own subgroup side by side in the discussion, so comparison_stated is true, and it calls the role of TMB 'still unclear', hence partial. Not neg: the rule never predicted a failure for the unselected population. EXTENTORCH's whole-exome biomarkers (low intratumour heterogeneity, HLA-A11+/B62-) are new rules, not a test of this one.

efficacy.magnitude_basis: no tumour growth suppression with anti-PD-1 alone in RP-48 OVA-LLO190 flank tumours vs 10-12 % objective response and no OS gain (CheckMate 032, 331, 451) with nivolumab alone
efficacy.confidence_note: Full text of the PMC author manuscript (PMC9844673) read in passages; the journal version may differ in wording (it spells 'PD1'). The antibody clone is not named in the passages read. The model carries engineered neoantigens (ovalbumin and listeriolysin peptide), which makes it more immunogenic than native SCLC, yet anti-PD-1 alone still did nothing. The patient side (CheckMate 331, registry results 2020-01-09) was known before the model was run.
efficacy.model: Rb1/Trp53 GEMM-derived syngeneic SCLC line (RP-48, engineered with OVA and LLO190 neoantigens) as flank tumours in C57BL/6 mice dosed with an anti-mouse PD-1 antibody, with or without the LSD1 inhibitor bomedemstat
efficacy.note: The first SCLC-specific immunocompetent mouse dosed with an anti-PD-1 antibody: alone it did not suppress tumour growth, reproducing the clinic's monotherapy inertness; it was built after that was known.
efficacy.short: SCLC mouse inert to anti-PD-1, as patients
efficacy.quote: Thus, while PD1 inhibition alone did not suppress tumor growth in this model, strong tumor growth inhibition was seen when combined with LSD1 inhibition.
efficacy.judgement: A separate track from the filed generic tumours: a different system (autochthonous-derived SCLC in an immunocompetent host) making a different prediction (SCLC-specific response). Retrodiction, so retro and never same: the paper opens from the clinic's modest checkpoint results and the model was run after CheckMate 032, 331 and 451 had reported. The pairing with the patient data is mine (the paper states the clinical premise but never juxtaposes its anti-PD-1-alone arm with a trial result), so comparison_stated false with the paper as model_src. The antibody is a rodent surrogate (product_in_model false). Sen 2019 (Cancer Discov) dosed anti-PD-L1 in Rb1/Trp53/p130 models, a sibling target outside the class, and Mahadevan 2021 dosed no PD-1 antibody, so neither opens the track earlier. The combination the model did find (anti-PD-1 plus bomedemstat) has no SCLC trial result, so no prospective entry follows yet.

efficacy.model: MC38 colon carcinoma in human PD-1 knock-in (humanised-PD-1) mice dosed with the product antibody itself: camrelizumab (SHR-1210) alone and with an IDO inhibitor (Tu 2019), and toripalimab at 0.3-10 mg/kg i.p. twice weekly (FDA BLA 761240 Study TR003)
efficacy.note: Product-dosed humanised-PD-1 MC38 model: camrelizumab (2019) and toripalimab 1-10 mg/kg (BLA 761240, 2023); its only SCLC tests are combination trials.
efficacy.short: Product-dosed knock-in MC38; only combination trials
efficacy.quote: In the MC38 xenograft model in hPD-1 transgenic mice, 25 in combination with the anti-PD-1 monoclonal antibody (SHR-1210) achieved a synergistic antitumor effect superior to each single agent.
efficacy.confidence_note: Tu 2019 read at abstract level (PMC6580535 exists, not read); the hPD-1 'transgenic' line is not named, so identity with the exon-2 knock-in used for toripalimab is by system type, and the abstract gives no single-agent number for SHR-1210. Toripalimab Study TR003 predates the 2018 NMPA approval but has no public date before the 2023 FDA review (bundle lines 4447-4464). Cheng 2025 (PMID 39541202) read at abstract level; NCT04012606 has no posted results (checked 2026-11-06); NCT03417895 results posted 2024-08-07.
efficacy.reason: Combination trials; model dosed antibody alone
efficacy.judgement: Split from mc38-mouse-pd1-blockade under this run's track-identity rule: a product-dosed antibody in a humanised-PD-1 host is a different system from a rat-chimeric surrogate (4H2) in wild-type mice, and it makes a different prediction (the product itself works, not just the mechanism). Camrelizumab (Tu 2019) and toripalimab (FDA 2023: 'Administration of toripalimab to MC38-bearing KI mice i.p. twice weekly at 0.3, 1, 3, or 10 mg/kg resulted in treatment-related decreased tumor growth at doses >= 1 mg/kg') are pooled on one track as the same system with the same prediction; model_src names the FDA review as the filed record of the system and model_filed is true on that account. No existing entry re-keys: the three mc38-mouse-pd1-blockade entries (2014 untested, 2016 same, 2020 contra) are all the nivolumab 4H2 surrogate; on merge, drop the clause 'later pooled with toripalimab's MC38 in human PD-1 knock-in mice' from that track's model text and the pooling sentence from its 2014 judgement. Status untested: the model dosed the antibody alone (Tu 2019's partner was an IDO inhibitor, not chemotherapy or apatinib; TR003 had no chemotherapy arm), and both SCLC tests are combinations, EXTENTORCH (toripalimab plus etoposide-platinum vs placebo plus etoposide-platinum, PFS and OS met) and PASSION (camrelizumab plus apatinib, single-arm ORR 34 %), so under this run's combination rule neither credits the model; both are recorded in patient_trials and change no status. Reviewer's call, as on the poppk-regimen-simulation track: a placebo-controlled add-on isolates the antibody, and under that reading this entry would be same (toripalimab, 2024). No dose entry is opened: the review does not set the model's >= 1 mg/kg threshold against clinical exposure, and the regimen question already sits on the poppk-regimen-simulation track.

patient_trials.quote: Compared with placebo, toripalimab improved investigator-assessed PFS (hazard ratio [HR], 0.67 [95% CI, 0.54-0.82]; P < .001), and significantly reduced the risk of death (HR, 0.80 [95% CI, 0.65-0.98]; P = .03).
In the QD cohort, confirmed ORR reached 34.0% (95% confidence interval: 20.9‒49.3), the median progression-free survival was 3.6 months, and the median overall survival was 8.4 months.

efficacy.model: Rb1/Trp53/Msh2 (RPM) mismatch-repair-deficient autochthonous SCLC GEMM with high tumour mutational burden, dosed at MRI-confirmed tumour manifestation with the anti-mouse PD-1 antibody RMP1-14 alone or with cisplatin/etoposide, against the Rb1/Trp53 (RP) parental strain
efficacy.population: MMR-deficient, high-TMB SCLC (about 15 % of cases per the paper), with the unselected RP strain as comparator
efficacy.note: Opens the track: an Msh2-deleted RP mouse built to carry the MMR signature and high TMB that about 15 % of human SCLC shows.
efficacy.quote: RPM tumors exhibited MMR deficiency, high tumor mutational burden (TMB), and an elevated load of candidate neoantigens, compared to RP lesions (p = 0.0106), suggesting increased immunogenicity.
efficacy.confidence_note: Full text read (PMC11564195; J Cancer Res Clin Oncol 150:496, epub 2024-11-14, PMID 39542886). The opener and the comparison are the same paper and year; the opener is kept so the track starts untested as the brief asks.
efficacy.judgement: Its own track: an autochthonous, MMR-deficient GEMM making a patient-level prediction (which SCLC responds) is a different system from the RP-48 OVA/LLO syngeneic flank model (sclc-rp-syngeneic-mouse, class-level) and from the sequencing-derived TMB rule (sclc-tmb-rule, no animal). The anti-PD-1 is the rodent surrogate RMP1-14 (product_in_model false); no regulator filed it.

efficacy.model: Rb1/Trp53/Msh2 (RPM) mismatch-repair-deficient autochthonous SCLC GEMM with high tumour mutational burden, dosed at MRI-confirmed tumour manifestation with the anti-mouse PD-1 antibody RMP1-14 alone or with cisplatin/etoposide, against the Rb1/Trp53 (RP) parental strain
efficacy.magnitude_basis: anti-PD-1 alone: median survival 51.5 vs 41 days in RPM mice (p = 0.0422) and no survival effect in RP mice, vs the higher nivolumab response and survival in the high-TMB tertile of CheckMate 032 (Hellmann 2018); no common quantity
efficacy.population: MMR-deficient, high-TMB SCLC (about 15 % of cases per the paper), with the unselected RP strain as comparator
efficacy.note: Built after CheckMate 032's TMB analysis: anti-PD-1 alone extends survival only in the high-TMB RPM mice, not in RP mice, reproducing the TMB rule.
efficacy.short: High-TMB SCLC mouse reproduces TMB rule
efficacy.quote: This notable response rate, which could be attributed to the elevated mutational load, aligns with recent clinical data indicating that high TMB bolsters the efficacy of immune checkpoint inhibition in SCLC patients
efficacy.confidence_note: Full text read (PMC11564195). The quoted sentence ends with the citation '(Hellmann et al. 2018)', omitted here. The paper summarises Hellmann 2018 in its introduction as benefit from 'a combination of two ICI agents' and in the discussion as checkpoint inhibition generally; Hellmann 2018 also reports the TMB effect for nivolumab alone, which is the member datum credited (the model dosed anti-PD-1 alone). Hellmann's tertile numbers were not re-read here; the patient-side quote is the draft's checker-verified abstract sentence. The paper itself cautions that clinical evidence for TMB as an ICI predictor is 'insufficient and contradictory' and that its regimens 'do not comply with standard clinical practice'.
efficacy.judgement: Retrodiction (decision 10): the model was built and run after Hellmann 2018 (CheckMate 032 TMB analysis) and Owonikoko 2021 (CheckMate 451 prespecified TMB subgroup), and the paper opens from Hellmann, so retro, never same. The comparison is stated by the paper (comparison_stated true, source_calls_it match). Patient-level: the prediction is that MMR-deficient / high-TMB SCLC benefits from anti-PD-1 while unselected SCLC does not, which is the sclc-tmb-rule track's rule re-derived in a mouse; it also reproduces the class-level monotherapy inertness (ICI alone did nothing in RP mice) that the sclc-rp-syngeneic-mouse track scores. endpoint_role primary with a caveat: the patient side is CheckMate 032's retrospective TMB analysis of its ORR primary endpoint, not a prespecified test. The combination arm is not scored: anti-PD-1 plus cisplatin/etoposide 'did not outperform chemotherapy alone' in RPM mice, the authors attribute that to toxicity, the only member combination trial (EXTENTORCH, toripalimab, unselected patients) went online the same day this paper did and is not a high-TMB datum, and the paper names only atezolizumab and durvalumab (non-members) for chemo-immunotherapy. First prospective test of this model's prediction would be a fresh entry.

patient_trials.quote: Efficacy of nivolumab ± ipilimumab was enhanced in patients with high tumor mutational burden.

efficacy.model: Rb1/Trp53/p130 (RPP) GEMM-derived syngeneic SCLC flank tumours in immunocompetent B6129F1 mice dosed with an anti-mouse PD-L1 antibody, alone and with PARP or CHK1 inhibitors (Sen 2019) or the WEE1 inhibitor adavosertib (Taniguchi 2022, which adds an Rb1/Trp53/MycT58A line)
efficacy.note: SCLC-genotype immunocompetent mouse dosed with anti-PD-L1, a sibling target outside the class; alone it was inert, as in the clinic, but no member was dosed.
efficacy.short: Anti-PD-L1 in SCLC mice; sibling class
efficacy.quote: PARP or CHK1 inhibition remarkably potentiated the antitumor effect of PD-L1 blockade and augmented cytotoxic T-cell infiltration in multiple immunocompetent SCLC in vivo models.
efficacy.confidence_note: Sen 2019 (Cancer Discov 9:646, epub 2019-02-18, PMID 30777870) read at abstract level: Europe PMC did not serve the PMC6563834 full text. Taniguchi 2022 (Cell Rep 39:110814, PMID 35584676) full text read: 'Treatment with anti-PD-L1 antibody alone was not efficacious in this model.' Neither passage read names the anti-PD-L1 clone.
efficacy.judgement: Recorded untested with the rule conflict stated, as the caller allowed: decision 12 (#69) scores a sibling-class surrogate dosed in the model as other, but decision 13 and lint make other safety-only, so in the efficacy cell this track cannot carry a status. What the model showed, anti-PD-L1 alone not efficacious in RPP tumours (Sen 2019, Taniguchi 2022), runs in the direction of CheckMate 032/331's monotherapy inertness, and Sen opens from 'only a minority of patients with SCLC respond to immune checkpoint blockade', so if the class boundary were widened to the PD-1/PD-L1 axis this would be a retrodiction (retro), not same. A separate track from sclc-rp-syngeneic-mouse (RP-48 OVA/LLO in C57BL/6 dosed with anti-PD-1), whose own judgement excludes Sen 2019 from opening it. The combination partners (PARP, CHK1, WEE1 inhibitors) have no SCLC trial result with a class member. Reviewer may delete the track if sibling-class systems are to be left out of efficacy entirely; the alternative is in considered_not_added.

safety.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading (PMID 10485649). The 2014 Opdivo label states 'immune-mediated disorders have been reported in PD-1 knockout mice' (section 8.1) and cites knockout mice in section 13.2, so model_filed is true.
safety.note: Aged PD-1-deficient mice develop lupus-like arthritis and glomerulonephritis: the class-level prediction of autoimmune harm, untested until a member reached SCLC patients.
safety.quote: Aged C57BL/6(B6)-PD-1(-/-) congenic mice spontaneously developed characteristic lupus-like proliferative arthritis and glomerulonephritis with predominant IgG3 deposition, which were markedly accelerated by introduction of a Fas mutation (lpr).
safety.judgement: The class-level autoimmunity model, opened at its first use; same track and slug as the HCC and NSCLC anti-PDCD1 tiles.

safety.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading (PMID 20624978). The 2014 Opdivo label section 13.2 carries the study ('M. tuberculosis-infected PD-1 knockout mice exhibit markedly decreased survival compared with wild-type controls'), so model_filed is true. No SCLC-specific tuberculosis datum for a member was sought in this run; nivolumab tuberculosis reactivation cases in other indications (reviewed in Eur J Cancer 2020, PMID 32375103) were not read and are a lead, not a score.
safety.model: Mycobacterium tuberculosis aerosol-infected PD-1 knockout (C57BL/6) mice read for survival, lung bacterial burden and inflammatory cytokines against wild-type controls; carried into the Opdivo label section 13.2
safety.note: PD-1 loss made Mtb-infected mice die faster with uncontrolled bacterial growth: an infection-exacerbation prediction no member has been compared against in SCLC.
safety.quote: PD-1-deficient mice showed dramatically reduced survival compared with wild-type mice.
safety.reason: No member TB comparison in SCLC
safety.judgement: Kept as its own track rather than folded into the autoimmunity knockout, as in the HCC tile: the same genotype but a different experimental system (aerosol Mtb challenge) making a different prediction (lethal failure to control a primary infection). Untested in this context; an imported comparison from nivolumab case series in other indications would be admissible under the transfer rule but was not verified within budget.

safety.magnitude_basis: no autoimmune disease in monkeys at exposures up to 42-fold the clinical AUC vs immune-mediated pneumonitis, colitis, hepatotoxicity, thyroid toxicity and nephritis as the commonest adverse events in nivolumab-treated patients
safety.population: Melanoma and other solid-tumour patients in the nivolumab BLA clinical programme (not SCLC)
safety.confidence_note: Review text obtained through the fc.py scrape; the quoted sentence is verbatim from the division director's memorandum (2014-12-04) and the primary review repeats it ('no evidence of autoimmune disease was observed in the monkey toxicology studies'). Imported from melanoma, the BLA's indication; the clinical trials the review refers to were mixed solid tumours.
safety.model: Cynomolgus monkey 4-week (weekly) and 13-week (twice-weekly) repeat-dose toxicology of nivolumab (up to 50 mg/kg; exposures at every dose above the 3 mg/kg Q2W clinical exposure)
safety.note: The FDA stated the miss: monkeys at 42-fold the clinical exposure showed only diffuse infiltrates while autoimmune disturbances were patients' commonest adverse events.
safety.short: Monkeys silent on the autoimmunity patients had
safety.quote: Monkeys did not develop any clear signs of the autoimmune toxicity seen in clinical trials with nivolumab, however, the generalized lymphocytic infiltration and increases in memory T cells do hint at the possibility of these types of toxicities.
safety.judgement: Contra by the transfer rule: a safety comparison stated by the regulator in another indication transfers, flagged imported_from. The species could have shown the lesion (another member's monkeys did on this track in the NSCLC tile), so the silence counts; the review's own 'hint' from infiltrates and memory T cells is a partial signal the status does not credit, recorded as source_calls_it miss because the FDA says monkeys did not show it. Opens the monkey safety track at the BLA, the same year the dose track opens.

safety.magnitude_basis: no immune-related events in monkeys at up to 50 mg/kg vs select (immune-type) treatment-related events in SCLC patients on nivolumab alone: skin 21.1 %, grade 3-4 pneumonitis 1.8 %, one encephalitis, one pneumonitis death (n = 109)
safety.population: Relapsed SCLC after two or more chemotherapy regimens (CheckMate 032 third-line nivolumab monotherapy, n = 109)
safety.confidence_note: Full text of Ready 2019 (JTO, epub 2018-10-10; PMC8050700) read in passages; the quote is verbatim. Antonia 2016 reported three treatment-related deaths (myasthenia gravis, renal failure, pneumonitis) earlier, but all in nivolumab plus ipilimumab cohorts, so the monotherapy cohort here anchors the year under the combination rule; a reviewer accepting combination harms would move the year to 2016.
safety.model: Cynomolgus monkey 4-week (weekly) and 13-week (twice-weekly) repeat-dose toxicology of nivolumab (up to 50 mg/kg; exposures at every dose above the 3 mg/kg Q2W clinical exposure)
safety.note: In SCLC itself: third-line nivolumab alone caused immune-type skin, pulmonary and neurologic events and one fatal pneumonitis in 109 patients; the monkeys had predicted none.
safety.short: Fatal pneumonitis in SCLC the monkeys never showed
safety.quote: One treatment-related death due to pneumonitis was noted.
safety.reason: Monkeys missed immune harms; knockout right
safety.judgement: Strengthens the imported 2014 contra with the in-context monotherapy datum; the pairing with the monkey data is mine (Ready 2019 does not discuss nonclinical work). Toripalimab's monkeys (NOAEL 100 mg/kg weekly for 26 weeks, no immune findings; FDA review 2023) belong on this track by identity and EXTENTORCH reports immune-related events, but the irAE rate was not read, so that member is not entered. Camrelizumab's reactive cutaneous capillary endothelial proliferation is a molecule-specific off-target harm scored on the HCC tile's receptor-proteome track; no camrelizumab SCLC safety datum was read beyond abstracts, so it is not entered here.

safety.magnitude_basis: lupus-like arthritis and glomerulonephritis in aged knockout mice vs immune-type pneumonitis (1.8 % grade 3-4, one fatal), encephalitis and skin reactions (21.1 %) in 109 SCLC patients on nivolumab alone
safety.population: Relapsed SCLC after two or more chemotherapy regimens (CheckMate 032 third-line nivolumab monotherapy, n = 109)
safety.confidence_note: Full text of Ready 2019 read in passages (PMC8050700); the quote is a verbatim clause. The paper reports 'select' treatment-related events, its term for immune-type events, without the words immune-mediated.
safety.note: Nivolumab alone in SCLC produced the autoimmune-type harms PD-1 loss in mice had foretold: pneumonitis (one fatal), encephalitis and skin reactions, in organs the knockout did not name.
safety.short: Immune harms in SCLC as knockout predicted
safety.quote: the most frequent grade 3 to 4 select TRAEs were pulmonary events (1.8% [n = 2, both pneumonitis])
safety.reason: Knockout right in direction, organs differ
safety.judgement: Pairing is mine. Same because a member produced immune-type events in SCLC patients given alone and the knockout's phenotype is autoimmunity; partial because the organ pattern (lung, brain, skin vs joints and kidney) and the incidence differ. Dated to the monotherapy cohort (epub 2018-10-10) for the same reason as the monkey entry; the 2016 combination-arm deaths would move it earlier if combination harms were admitted.
